Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a SINGLE tiny pixel-art battlefield remains sprite for the existing tactical dungeon game.
Input 1 is the exact albino troglodyte to transform; input 2 is the real game screen and is a STYLE, CAMERA and SCALE reference only.
Preserve the distinctive broad snout, squat chunky proportions and simple hard pixel clusters of the troglodyte. The character is a small creature, roughly two thirds the height of a warrior.
Deliver one isolated object, transparent RGBA background, no tile, no pedestal, no scene, no UI, no words or labels.
Native low-resolution pixel-art appearance: about 64x40 occupied logical pixels, magnified with perfectly square hard pixels, deliberate sparse clusters, only 10-14 flat colors, one or two shadow tones per material. No subpixel smoothing, gradients, blur, painterly texture, soft shadow, glossy highlights or thin high-resolution detail.
Shallow three-quarter overhead game camera consistent with a 2:1 isometric floor. Remains rest FLAT ON THE FLOOR. A narrow hard-edged dark contact cluster touches the underside, no detached oval shadow, no hovering. Muted pale ivory, dusty mauve-gray, deep charcoal outlines; a small restrained dark brick-red blood accent for fresh corpses, never a large red puddle. Readability and simplicity take priority over detail. Fresh corpse variant 1: the SAME small albino troglodyte lying dead on its left side, broad head at lower-left, heavy back and hip at upper-right, forelimbs slack in front, hindlimbs folded. Preserve a recognisable complete compact body and weight on the ground, similar to the final C2 collapse in reference 2. Closed eyes, slightly open jaw; small dried dark-red mark below cheek. No exposed organs or dismemberment.
